entries.title: Does AI Reinforce Gender Stereotypes? Gender Bias in Job Descriptions Generated by 40+ Large Language Models
entries.summary: An audit of 48 language models compared 4,608 job descriptions generated from matched gender-neutral and gender-coded titles. Some measured differences persisted despite prompt changes; salary differences were not robust across all analyses, and applicant outcomes were not measured.
entries.why_it_matters: When using AI to draft vacancies, start with gender-neutral job titles and audit the resulting language and salary suggestions rather than relying on prompt corrections alone.

entries.title: When Does Workload Undermine Innovative Behavior? The Joint Moderating Roles of Empowering Leadership and Perceived Organizational Support
entries.summary: Across three waves of data from 349 employees and 30 supervisors at one Chinese firm, workload was associated with greater exhaustion and lower innovative behavior. The observational design does not establish that workload caused either outcome.
entries.why_it_matters: When investigating a decline in innovation, analyze workload and exhaustion alongside employees’ perceptions of managerial and organizational support rather than treating innovation scores in isolation.

entries.title: Between support and effort: how managerial need support and employee need crafting longitudinally associate with employee basic psychological needs
entries.summary: In a three-wave study of US and UK employees, managerial support and employees’ own job-crafting behaviors had different associations with autonomy, competence, and relatedness. Of 796 initial participants, 500 completed the final wave; the associations do not establish causation.
entries.why_it_matters: In an employee-listening program, measure autonomy, competence, and connection separately, alongside manager support and employees’ opportunities to shape their work, rather than relying on a single needs score.

entries.title: When AI thinks about culture: comparing language-based and empirical measures of individualism–collectivism
entries.summary: Researchers compared five language models’ country-level cultural estimates with a survey-based index covering 102 countries and territories. Despite strong overall alignment, the models systematically overstated Western individualism and understated it in Confucian East Asian societies relative to the benchmark.
entries.why_it_matters: Before using AI-generated cultural profiles to design a multinational employee survey or management program, compare them with current, context-specific evidence and avoid treating national averages as individual traits.
